title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-warmup-incident-debug-notes
content:
Goal: capture commands tried, quick error snippets, hypotheses and immediate next steps for the recent capacity thrash / warmup incident on the dedicated GPU pool (us-west-2, g4dn->p4 mix).

Summary of incident (high level):
- Time window: 2024-11-01 22:10 - 2024-11-01 23:40 UTC.
- Symptom: rapid scale-up/down churn (capacity thrash) during a scheduled traffic spike + rollout that increased pod startup failures and cold-Latency for requests.
- Impact: several customer requests hit 500s or ~10-20s cold-starts; autoscaler overshot capacity then immediately scaled down, causing repeated warmup penalties.

What I observed (notes from the on-call terminal):
- HPA/Custom autoscaler behavior looked noisy: scaling events every ~2-4 minutes during the window.
- Many new nodes came up but kubelet reported ImagePullBackOff or CrashLoopBackOff for the serving container on some instances (mostly p4d instances).
- We saw repeated "KvCache miss" spikes in the runtime logs while pods were initializing, causing long preparation time per pod (~30-60s).
- Autoscaler config: target-utilization 0.6, cooldown 3m, warmup_seconds set to 45 (maybe too low).

Commands and queries I ran (timestamps approximate):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-serving -o wide --show-labels | grep warmup  # list warmup pods
- kubectl logs -n dedicated-serving pod/serve-xyz-init -c init -f --since=1h  # init container logs showed artifact download timeouts
- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-23 | sed -n '1,120p'  # check node taints/capacity
- kubectl get events -n dedicated-serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 200  # surf events for crash/oom/pull errors
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:pool,Values=dedicated-gpu Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running --region us-west-2  # match up with node joins
- curl -sS http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason[5m])  # quick metric check

Error / log snippets collected: (copied raw lines)
- "Warning  Failed  12s  kubelet, ip-10-0-1-23  Failed to pull image \"registry.redwood.internal/serve:release-2024-11-01\": context deadline exceeded"
- "serve_runtime ERROR kv_cache: prefix not found, initializing KV state (cold)"
- "autoscaler INFO scale_down: candidate=pool-3, last_scale_time=2024-11-01T22:12:10Z, desire_replicas=2, current_replicas=8, cooldown_remaining=30s"
- "init_container WARN download: artifact fetch timed out after 20s, retrying (attempt 2)"
- "node-controller INFO node_join: ip-10-0-1-23 type=p4d.xlarge labels:gpu-type=p4d,zone=us-west-2a"

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Artifact download / init container slowness + image pull throttling leads to pods not reporting Ready quickly -> autoscaler sees low utilization and keeps scaling up then scales down when nodes temporarily look idle. Warmup_seconds too short for our warmup profile.
2) Mixed instance types (g4dn + p4) with different startup times cause capacity mismatch and scheduling bin-packing issues; scheduler back-and-forth places pods on slower nodes causing churn.
3) KV cache and model warmup cost (heavy CPU/GPU memory ops) prolongs pod readiness beyond cooldown window; autoscaler treats them as idle and scales down.
4) Intermittent registry latency (internal registry) causes ImagePullBackOff and delayed start.

Data points to validate hypotheses:
- correlate pod Ready times with autoscaler decisions (pull timestamps from events and compare to scale events in autoscaler logs).
- check registry metrics (ECR/registry internal) for spike in latency/3xx/5xx around 22:10-22:30 UTC.
- check warmup_seconds vs observed median pod startup (init container + runtime warmup) per instance type.
- inspect schedule binpack logs and scheduler events for repeated pod evictions/unschedulable messages.

Actionable next steps (short term):
- Bump warmup_seconds to 180s for the dedicated pool as a temporary mitigation (will reduce churn). Put change behind feature-flag for quick rollback.
- Add a pre-pull step for model artifacts in user-init to reduce init container jitter (experiment).
- Increase cooldown window for autoscaler to 10m to avoid oscillation while we investigate.
- Add a Prometheus dashboard: "dedicated_pool_startup_latency" (init start -> pod Ready) split by instance-type and image-pull duration.
- Open a ticket to infra registry team with logs: attach image pull error lines and request check for rate-limiting or ECR response latencies. (see linked JIRA-INC-1427)

Longer-term / follow-ups:
- Consider separating instance types into different node pools (fast warmup vs cheap) and use node affinity/schedulingPolicies to put latency-sensitive models on fast nodes.
- Evaluate warming strategy: keep a small number of prewarmed pods per pool that always stay Ready and get evicted last. Estimate cost tradeoffs.
- Improve autoscaler heuristics: recognize "initializing" pod states and delay scale-down while a portion of pods are in warmup states.
- Work with model team to quantify KV-cache load and provide light-weight warmup that reduces per-pod initialization time.

Notes / random traces (for breadcrumbs):
- Found pattern: autoscaler scale_up at 22:12, new nodes join 22:14-22:16, pods stuck in init until 22:20, autoscaler scale_down at 22:22 (thinks idle) -> repeat.
- One p4 instance had docker daemon restart during join (system journal shows docker.service crash). Possible culprit for some of the CrashLoopBackOff.
- Observed spike in external registry 429s at 22:15 in cloud logs.

Things I want from others:
- @Samir: can you pull ECR registry logs for 22:00-23:00 UTC and check 429/5xx counts?
- @Maya: can infra ops check the AMI across p4 nodes for docker stability and kernel messages around 22:10-22:30?
- @Jordan: can you extract autoscaler decision log for pool=dedi-gpu-01 and paste the scale event window (22:00-23:30)?

TODO (short):
- [ ] apply warmup_seconds=180 in staging and run load test
- [ ] create prometheus panel for startup latency
- [ ] attach init container logs to JIRA ticket
- [ ] run node image validation on p4 AMI in canary AZ

If anything else comes up I'll append here. This is intentionally messy; keeping raw commands and log lines helps reconstruct sequence during postmortem.

-- Avery
